### Eternally Satisfying Water
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/eternally-satisfying-water
Passage: John 4:10-15
Points:
- Jesus' fatigue and thirst at Jacob's well reveal His genuine human nature.
- The Samaritan woman came alone at midday because she was ostracized by her community.
- Jesus ignored social and ethnic taboos to initiate a conversation with an outcast.
- While she thought only of physical water, Jesus offered the gift of eternal life.
- Worldly sources leave the soul longing, but Christ provides everlasting spiritual satisfaction.

### Monday Morning Meditation on Thirst
Author: John Piper
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/monday-morning-meditation-on-thirst
Passage: John 4:14
Points:
- Believers often experience ongoing spiritual dryness and wonder why they still feel thirsty.
- Jesus does not eradicate our capacity to thirst, which would end our need for Him.
- Instead, the water Christ imparts establishes a living, interior spring inside the believer.
- The spring is permanently present so we can drink from it whenever thirst arises.
- Christian living is an ongoing rhythm of rising need met by Christ's repeated satisfaction.

### Running on Empty
Author: Christina Patterson
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/beloved-women/beloved-women-february-22-2021.html
Passage: John 4:13-14
Points:
- Just as vehicles run out of fuel, human bodies and souls inevitably run out of energy.
- People frequently attempt to soothe internal depletion with physical habits, binge-watching, or food.
- Relying on physical substitutes for spiritual needs leaves the soul drier and emptier than before.
- Jesus alone supplies the living water that satisfies the soul's deepest longings.
- Whenever we recognize we are depleted, we must run directly to Christ for renewal.

### The Living Water We All Need
Author: Alexis A. Goring
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/the-living-water-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: John 4:10
Points:
- Sweet drinks fail to quench physical dehydration, just as earthly pursuits fail our spirits.
- Jesus deliberately arranged a solitary encounter with an outcast woman carrying painful baggage.
- Christ looked past ethnic hostility and moral failure to offer her salvation and living water.
- Humans constantly chase temporary counterfeits to fill a void only God can satisfy.
- Embracing a personal relationship with Jesus quenches our spiritual thirst for eternity.
